_: Provenance for the generated footage in clipsrc/generated/.
Every clip is image-to-video conditioned on TWO approved plates: `from` is
its first frame and `to` is its last. That is not a stylistic choice, it is
what makes the footage safe to drop into this table. VIDEO.md section 6 asks
for the first frame to be locked to an approved plate so drift is bounded
inside one clip; locking the last frame as well means a clip also ENDS on a
picture that already exists as a still, so <Clip> can cut away to it with no
jump and a browser that cannot play the video shows the right frame anyway.
These models are not deterministic and the seed is not exposed, so this file
records how a clip was ordered, not how to reproduce it byte for byte. The
mp4 in clipsrc/generated/ is the source asset; this is its receipt.
Re-fetch with: node scripts/fetch-generated.mjs [name...]
chosen: Kling 3 Omni over PixVerse V6, decided by measurement rather than taste.
Both were given the identical rest->pull pair and the identical prompt, and
scripts/measure-drift.mjs was run over every frame of each result:
worst translation   mean residual   source   credits
Translation is the column that mattered. The reel window is a hole the DOM
bands show through, so a casting that wanders is bands leaking past the
brass, and while scripts/lib/lock.mjs takes the wander out afterwards, the
less there is to take out the less the frame has to be pushed around. The
residuals are effectively tied, and both sit at about the level the approved
still plates already differ from each other by, which is the real bar.

pull.prompt: Locked-off tripod camera. Absolutely static framing: no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no dolly, no handheld drift, no parallax. 1899 saloon at night. A heavy cast-iron three-reel slot machine stands on a mahogany bar top; the casting, its scrollwork, its brass payout plate and its coin cup do not move or rotate by a single pixel. THE ONLY MOTION IS THE ARM: the man's right hand grips the nickel-plated ball on the end of the lever and hauls it down through its arc until it strikes the hard stop at the bottom; forearm tendons tighten, the loose linen sleeve drags and settles. The dark rectangular reel window in the face of the machine stays absolutely black, empty, and perfectly still - nothing appears inside it. The hanging oil lamp at far left flickers faintly. The men in the dark behind the bar barely stir. Warm amber lamplight falling off hard into blackness, 35mm film grain.

idle.prompt: Locked-off tripod camera. Absolutely static framing: no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no dolly, no handheld drift. 1899 saloon at night, the quiet moment between pulls. Nothing dramatic happens and nothing is ever completely still. The hanging oil lamp at far left gutters: its flame leans, dips low enough to brown the light across the whole bar, then climbs back, so the warm pool of light on the mahogany slowly breathes darker and brighter. Smoke drifts through the beam. The men standing in the dark behind the bar shift their weight, one turns his head slowly, another lifts a glass, a shoulder moves; they stay in shadow and nobody reacts to anything. The player's right hand rests on the nickel lever ball, the forearm rising and falling very slightly with his breathing. THE MACHINE DOES NOT MOVE: the heavy cast-iron three-reel slot machine, its scrollwork, its brass payout plate and its coin cup are perfectly still, not one pixel of drift or rotation. The dark rectangular reel window in its face stays absolutely black, empty and perfectly still - nothing appears inside it. The shot ends exactly as it began. Warm amber lamplight, deep shadow, 35mm film grain.

_: The four shots below are the opening, and they are the one place in this
project where the camera is allowed to move. Everything at the table is
locked off because the DOM has to stay registered to the picture; the
opening has nothing laid over it, so it can be a camera instead of a
plate. That is also why three of the four have no `to`: a shot that is
going somewhere cannot be asked to end where it started.
They exist to replace pushIn(), a Ken Burns crop that stood in for a
dolly. A crop of a still cannot produce parallax, so the fake move read
as a zoom on a photograph, and it was also the thing blowing the first
screen budget: the synthetic motion had no real structure to predict
from, so intro.sm.webm encoded at 726 KB against a 400 KB ceiling.
THIS SHOT REPLACED AN EXTERIOR. The opening used to begin outside, on a
dark frontier street, pushing in toward the light coming out of a
doorway (historyId Qprx2IsSmHoAcEFonBux, plate clipsrc/intro_street.jpg,
both now deleted). It was the best-looking shot in the project and it
was the wrong first shot: this table is about a room full of people and
what they do when you win or lose, and a building cannot be noisy. The
opening now starts already inside, in the loud part of the evening.
The plate this is conditioned on was made on OpenArt too - Nano Banana
Pro image2image, historyId hjvLMICNi3idzcX0FOGi, conditioned on the new
room plate below and on machine_rest so the light matches the table.
Three candidates came back and the choice was measured, not eyeballed:
mean R-B of +13.2 against the approved machine plate's +13.9, where the
two rejects sat at +18.4 and +31.0. See slots/README.md.
intro_bar.prompt:
A slow, steady dolly drifting forward and slightly to the right along the length of the bar in a crowded 1899 saloon at night. The camera moves at an unhurried walking pace, as if it has just come through the door into the noise of the room. No handheld shake, no cuts.

The room is alive and everyone in it is doing something. The men along the brass rail talk to each other with real movement - heads turning, mouths working, hands gesturing, shoulders shifting as they lean in to be heard. Two of them raise glasses and touch them together. The bartender in the white apron tips the bottle and pours into the row of shot glasses on the bar top. The man at the piano works his hands along the keys. The man beside him laughs, head back. Somebody drains a beer and sets it down on the wood. Cigar smoke rolls slowly through the beams of the hanging oil lamps, and the lamp flames gutter and steady.

Keep the exposure and grade exactly as the first frame: warm amber pools falling off hard into near-black, thick smoke, heavy 35mm film grain, shallow depth of field. Nobody walks into or out of frame and nobody looks at the camera. No text or lettering appears. No cuts.

intro_room.prompt:
A slow dolly travelling forward down the length of a busy 1899 saloon gambling hall at night, past the occupied card tables, toward the far end of the room. Steady and unhurried, no handheld shake, no cuts. The camera passes under the hanging oil lamps and they gutter as it goes by.

The near half of the room is working: the dealer's hands move over the green baize and he slides a card out; a seated player leans back in his chair and turns his head to say something; a man at the bar on the right lifts his glass and drinks; the bartender tips a bottle and pours; men standing in groups shift their weight and talk, heads turning to each other. Cigar smoke rolls through every lamp beam.

But the crowd at the dead end of the room, packed around the lit cast-iron slot machine, stays almost completely still - they are watching it, and only a shoulder or a hat moves. The contrast is the point of the shot: a noisy room with one silent knot of people in it. The machine at the far end stays the brightest thing in frame and the eye is drawn down the room to it.

Keep the exposure and grade exactly as the first frame: warm amber pools falling off hard into near-black, heavy 35mm film grain, shallow depth of field. Nobody walks into or out of frame and nobody looks at the camera. No text or lettering. No cuts.

intro_band.prompt: Extreme macro, a slow lateral tracking move along a printed paper slot-machine reel band lying flat on a worn workbench in a dark back room, 1899. The camera slides slowly sideways along the strip, revealing symbol after symbol - and one place where a symbol has been carefully cut out of the paper with a blade and replaced, the edges of the patch just visible. A single work lamp rakes across the surface from one side so the paper fibres and the knife edge catch the light. Faint smoke in the air. Tiny depth of field, only the strip in focus, everything beyond it falling into blackness. Nothing else in the room moves; no hands enter the frame. 35mm film grain, warm low light. No cuts.

_: The LAST shot of the four, and the only one of the four with a `to`.
It is not conditioned at both ends in order to join up with a cut -
nothing follows it, the opening fades out of this shot and hands over
to the machine picker. It is conditioned at both ends so that the
machine in the opening is the SAME machine the player sits down at: a
push that is not pinned at its end arrives on some other casting, and
the plate this is pinned to is the one the table opens on.
It used to be shot three, with the macro of the band after it. The
order was swapped when the exterior came out: the screen after this
one asks which machine you want, so the last thing the player looks at
before they get control should be a machine.
intro_machine.prompt: A very slow, very slight dolly push toward a heavy cast-iron three-reel slot machine standing on a saloon bar top in 1899, with a man's hand already closed around the nickel-plated ball of its lever. Almost imperceptible movement - the frame tightens by only a few percent and comes to rest exactly where it started, as if the camera leaned in to look and then settled. The hanging oil lamp at the left gutters. Smoke drifts. The men behind the bar stay in deep shadow and barely stir. The hand does not pull the lever; it only holds it. The dark rectangular reel window in the face of the machine stays absolutely black and empty. Warm amber lamplight falling off hard into blackness, 35mm film grain, shallow depth of field. No cuts, no shake.
